title: Trees: Serialize and Deserialize
oneLiner: Turn a binary tree into a string and back. A preorder walk that writes a marker for every missing child records enough to rebuild the exact shape.
keyTakeaway: Write the tree in preorder and emit a marker such as # for every null child. Because every null is recorded, one traversal fixes the shape: reading the tokens back in the same order, each value is a node whose left subtree comes next, then its right subtree, and # ends a branch. Both directions are O(n).
explanation:
Write Serialize(root), which turns a binary tree into a string, and Deserialize(data), which turns that string back into the same tree. The format is yours to choose. The grader builds a tree, runs Deserialize(Serialize(tree)) and checks the result has exactly the same values and shape, so test trees include negative and multi-digit values and lopsided shapes.

Why one traversal is enough here when Build From Preorder and Inorder needed two: that problem had no record of where children were missing. Write the nulls down and the ambiguity disappears. A preorder walk with # for null turns [1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5] into "1,2,#,#,3,4,#,#,5,#,#".

Serialize: if the node is null, append #. Otherwise append its value, then serialize the left child, then the right child. Join the tokens with commas; a separator is what lets -12 and 34 stay distinct values.

Deserialize: split on commas and read tokens with a running index. read(): take the next token; if it is #, return null. Otherwise make a node from it, set its left child to read(), then its right child to read(), and return it. The recursion consumes tokens in exactly the order Serialize produced them, so it rebuilds the same tree.

Both directions touch each node and each null once. A tree with n nodes has n + 1 null children, so the string has 2n + 1 tokens: O(n) time and O(n) space, plus O(h) recursion. A level-order (BFS) format with null markers, like the one this site uses to print trees, works just as well.

The visualization deserializes "1,2,#,#,3,4,#,#,5,#,#" token by token.

visualizationSteps.message: Serialize([1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5]) wrote "1,2,#,#,3,4,#,#,5,#,#". Now read it back, one token at a time, in the same preorder.
Token 0 is 1: make it the root. The next tokens describe its left subtree, then its right.
Token 1 is 2: make it the left child of 1. The next tokens describe its left subtree, then its right.
Token 2 is #: the left child of 2 is empty, so this branch ends.
Token 3 is #: the right child of 2 is empty, so this branch ends.
Token 4 is 3: make it the right child of 1. The next tokens describe its left subtree, then its right.
Token 5 is 4: make it the left child of 3. The next tokens describe its left subtree, then its right.
Token 6 is #: the left child of 4 is empty, so this branch ends.
Token 7 is #: the right child of 4 is empty, so this branch ends.
Token 8 is 5: make it the right child of 3. The next tokens describe its left subtree, then its right.
Token 9 is #: the left child of 5 is empty, so this branch ends.
Token 10 is #: the right child of 5 is empty, so this branch ends.
All 11 tokens used: 5 nodes and 6 null markers (n + 1 of them). Same tree as before serializing.

pythonHarnessPreamble:
null = None

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val
        self.left = None
        self.right = None

def build_level_order_tree(values):
    # Builds a tree from a level-order list; null (None) marks a missing child.
    if not values or values[0] is None:
        return None
    root = TreeNode(values[0])
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(values):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if values[i] is not None:
            node.left = TreeNode(values[i])
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(values) and values[i] is not None:
            node.right = TreeNode(values[i])
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root

def tree_to_list(root):
    # The tree as a level-order list with None for missing children, trailing Nones trimmed.
    result = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            result.append(None)
            continue
        result.append(node.val)
        queue.append(node.left)
        queue.append(node.right)
    while result and result[-1] is None:
        result.pop()
    return result
recognitionSignals: Store, send or copy a tree (or any linked structure) and get the identical structure back.
Rebuilding a shape from a single traversal: you must record the empty children.
gotchas: Without null markers, different trees serialize to the same string.
Without a separator, values like 1 and 23 run together as 123.
In Deserialize, the token index must be shared across the whole recursion (a field, a nonlocal or an iterator), not a parameter copied into each call.
confusableWith: Build From Preorder and Inorder rebuilds from two traversals without null markers; here one traversal is enough because the nulls are written down.
Clone Graph copies a structure in memory; serialization is the same walk but writes to text in between.

complexity.note: Each direction visits every node once and every null child once (n + 1 of them), so the string has 2n + 1 tokens. Space is the string and the token list, O(n), plus O(h) recursion.
